author: Patrick Elwood
title: Drone search and rescue reunites owner with lost husky in Chicago's northwest suburbs - NewsBreak
text:
By Patrick Elwood Alonzo Small ,
2 hours ago
LAKEMOOR, Ill. ( WGN ) — Help arrived from the sky by way of a high-tech rescue for a beloved lost dog who was lost and alone in Chicago’s northwest suburbs.
Valorie Revere has since been reunited with her 12-year-old husky named ‘Bandit,’ who disappeared Saturday, June 13, after surviving several days stuck in the mud in a cold marsh in Lakemoor.
Bandit made a dash when a door at Revere’s home was left open.
Revere contacted Pero Radulovic of Pero’s Backwoods Drone Search and Rescue. By Sunday afternoon, Radulovic had been in the area for five hours, searching for the Bandit to no avail. He went back on Monday, about 3 a.m. Using his drone with thermal imaging, Radulovic located the missing dog.
With assistance from the Lakemoor Police Department and the McHenry Township Fire Protection District, first responders rescued Bandit from the muddy marsh. Rescuers said his head was just above the water, and he was covered in ticks.
Reflecting on the rescue to WGN-TV , Radulovic expressed his love for the job.
“This is kind of my job. I love to do this and I love to save people’s pets, so when I finally came across Bandit, I was overjoyed and happy that [Revere] was able to trust Pero’s Backwoods Drone Search and Rescue to find Bandit,” he said.
First responders rushed the rescued pup to a nearby veterinary clinic, as Bandit was in critical condition and needed urgent care to the tune of $12,000.
Revere started a GoFundMe, but within 24 hours, Bandit made a remarkable recovery.
“They were very surprised at how well he was doing the very next day and how his blood work came back. So, he’s still not out of the woods. He still has a fever. He still has an infection. He still has an issue with his liver. The kidneys are making progress…but he doesn’t have to go to critical care,” Revere added.
Bandit is already a trooper when it comes to adversity, Revere says, after the dog lost an eye last year due to glaucoma.
“We call him the ‘One-eyed Bandit’ now, but he is such a fighter,” she said.
As for the GoFundMe, which has since been shut down, Revere said Valorie is thankful to everyone who helped find him and to the people who donated. The money raised, she adds, will go to paying the much smaller vet bill for Bandit.
